answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate combined with incumbent refusal to reopen pricing leaves renew_incumbent and negotiate_terms non-viable. Memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor executed onboarding quickly with accurate invoicing on a prior engagement, establishing baseline execution credibility. Memory_c3 shows second-sourcing's value in shortage resilience, but adding capacity doesn't close the 18% gap; switching does. Memory_c6 shows long-term commitments can unlock pricing, but we have 14 days and no negotiation leverage. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate in one move. However, the assembly line at 94% utilization creates material downstream risk if the switch introduces any delivery variance or quality deviation. Verification of memory_c2 (prior low-cost execution) and memory_c4 (negotiation leverage recovery) will confirm whether low-cost vendor reliability is proven or negotiation could still move the incumbent. Standard experiment scale (time-boxed trial, contingency to revert) mitigates the 94% utilization risk. If the vendor performs, cost cuts; if not, we have 14 days to pivot. This is the least bad option under the constraints.
